item.title: North Carolina student wins top award for free tool mapping wildlife roadkill hotspots
item.description: Aaryan Ghorpade, a North Carolina student, has triumphed in a national competition with EcoRoute, a project that tracks wildlife-vehicle collision hotspots across the U.S. This innovative online tool gathers collision data and produces heat maps to assist transportation agencies in improving road safety. EcoRoute also encourages community involvement, allowing users to report wildlife sightings. Ghorpade envisions further enhancements and plans to partner with wildlife conservation organizations in his state.

item.title: Stephen King's Maine mansion becomes a literary archive, with $2,500 writers' retreats next door
item.description: Stephen King and Tabitha have innovatively turned their Bangor residence into a unique archive and retreat for writers. This initiative offers aid and an inspiring atmosphere, allowing selected authors to immerse themselves in their work. The nearby Brown Mansion will serve as an additional haven, benefitting a variety of literary talents, including educators and Maine local writers.

item.title: What led to Susie Wiles' firing within 3 days of Trump's midterm loss? 'Ice maiden' was Trump's longest serving chief of staff

item.title: Meryl Streep backs women's history education as two teachers earn award for AP course campaign
item.description: Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams from Sacred Heart Preparatory have pioneered an Advanced Placement course focused on women's history, garnering endorsement from 100 esteemed universities and colleges. This initiative underscores the vital role women have played throughout history. An eminent gala in Chicago on November 6, 2026, will unveil the inaugural Meryl Streep Educator Award, with proceeds dedicated to bolstering educational resources for women's history.

item.title: London councillors reject Berkeley Homes plan after affordable housing offer falls from 40% to 12%
item.description: Southwark Council's planning committee voted unanimously against Berkeley Homes' revised plans for the Bermondsey Place development. The housebuilder proposed reducing affordable housing from 40 percent to just 12 percent, causing strong local opposition. Council members expressed concerns about the long timeline for home completion and questioned the developer's financial figures. Berkeley Homes highlighted rising costs and council fees as reasons for the reduced affordable housing offer.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Court upholds sale of divorced Arkansas woman's property share after her bankruptcy filing.
item.description: In a landmark ruling, a federal appeals court upheld the sale of a divorced woman's stake in property located in Arkansas. The decision favored her bankruptcy trustee, overcoming objections posed by her ex-husband. He contended that the buyer's good faith was not adequately proven in prior hearings but failed to voice this concern earlier. Consequently, the property transaction with Blue Sun Capital LLC is deemed legally binding.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2017, Gaten Matarazzo helped form a charity; nine years later, its partners issued 37 care tips
item.description: Cleidocranial dysplasia (CCD) affects bone and dental development in patients and requires specialized care. A recent study established 37 expert recommendations for diagnosing and managing this rare condition effectively. These guidelines emphasize the importance of coordinated care among various specialists and regular monitoring. Gaten Matarazzo, who has CCD, advocates for better recognition and treatment of the disorder. CCD Smiles organization aims to support patients through awareness and research initiatives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California condo parking dispute ends after decade; court rejects $292,544 legal fee claim
item.description: In a contentious parking dispute in Orange County, condominium owners WCST Enterprises and Berit Ling faced off in court. Ultimately, the court ruled in favor of WCST, affirming its claim to garage space 38G-a. However, despite the legal victory, WCST could not reclaim its substantial legal fees of $292,544, as these claims did not meet California statutes for fee recovery.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 125-year-old Idaho ranch gets permanent protection
item.description: A conservation easement has been established on the Flying A Ranch in Idaho to protect the land. This easement allows the Atchley family to continue their farming operations while preventing future development. The agreement also supports a crucial wildlife migration corridor for mule deer and various other species. Previous efforts to protect the ranch were led by Clen Atchley, who passed away in 2024.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: New research rules out the theory of Stonehenge Altar Stone's Northeast Scottish Origin
item.description: Researchers continue to explore the origins of the Altar Stone at Stonehenge, which weighs approximately six tonnes. Recent studies suggested a possible origin from northeast Scotland, but findings have complicated this theory. A new international team's research found no matching source from the Scottish locations they examined, narrowing possibilities down. Previous assumptions about the Altar Stone's Welsh origins have been challenged by new geological insights.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Brisbane Library House Auction: former private library cleared for sale; rebuild interest grows
item.description: After years of neglect, a three-bedroom home in Wynnum, Brisbane, has undergone a remarkable transformation. This property, once filled with a vast collection of books and memorabilia, required extensive teamwork to clear out its contents and evict wildlife. Now, it's being showcased as an exciting renovation or rebuilding opportunity in a sought-after neighborhood, with an auction date set for November 14, 2026, drawing potential buyers eager to invest.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: Louisiana woman fights uncle over mother's estate for 13 years; court revives part of lawsuit
item.description: A Louisiana woman accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of her late mother's estate to himself and businesses linked to him. More than 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived her claims concerning his handling of the estate but upheld the dismissal of other claims. It also cancelled a $10,000 damages award and ordered further proceedings.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: For more than 60 years, visitors walked through a cave in Spain; now 280 motifs identified
item.description: A remarkable archaeological find at Cova de la Font Major has revealed 280 Palaeolithic engravings, showcasing diverse motifs of animals and geometric shapes. This challenges the previously held notion that cave art was scarce in northeastern Iberia, where only two pieces were known. These engravings suggest the existence of unique artistic traditions independent of the famous Franco-Cantabrian region, offering new insights into the cultural practices of Ice Age Europe.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Twenty black grouse were moved from the North Pennines to the North York Moors in 2024
item.description: In a remarkable conservation achievement, black grouse have successfully hatched chicks in North York Moors after a long absence of 200 years. In 2024, 20 black grouse were moved from North Pennines as part of a dedicated effort that includes habitat restoration and management of predators. Reports indicate a notable rise in the number of displaying males, with plans for further translocations underway to bolster their population even more.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
